To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have crystallized VanA, a key enzyme involved in bacterial resistance to glycopeptide antibiotics, in the presence of an inhibitor analogue, and we have obtained diffraction data to at least 1.8 A.
VanA is a 50 kDa enzyme that is responsible for the biosynthesis of the D-alanyl-D-lactate pentapeptide that is attached to the D-alanine-D-Ala terminus of bacterial cell wall peptidoglycan.
we crystallized and solved the structure of VanA, a key enzyme in bacterial resistance to the antibiotic vancomycin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of resistance of bacteria to vancomycin and related glycopeptide antibiotics.
the molecular basis of resistance to glycopeptide antibiotics in Enterococcus faiceum BM4147 and the structure of D-alanine:D-lactate ligases.
the elucidation of the molecular basis of glycopeptide antibiotic resistance, in particular the molecular mechanism of the VanA ligase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crystals are of a high quality for the determination of the structure by X-ray analysis.
this is the first time that a D-alanine-Dlactate ligase has been purified, crystallized and shown to be active.

the crystallographic analysis of this enzyme should provide a detailed molecular basis for the mechanism of action of the glycopeptide antibiotics and the basis for resistance to these antibiotics.
we have crystallized VanA and have obtained a crystallographic data set to a high resolution.
the VanA protein has been successfully overexpressed and purified to homogeneity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VanA crystallized only in the presence D-alanyl-phosphinate and that the phosphinate was essential for crystal formation.
the VanA ligase is a dimeric protein with two active sites per molecule.
VanA is a dimeric enzyme and that the dimer interface involves residues that have previously been implicated in substrate binding.
